quotes.text: And here's the hard truth. AI won't save you from bad architecture. Copilot or semantic search can't invent metadata that doesn't exist.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States plainly why information architecture is a prerequisite for useful Copilot results.

quotes.text: The second rule, avoid deep folders. Folders are brittle mazes. They break when you move things around, and after a reorg they collapse into bizarre half paths no one remembers.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: Information architecture isn't ornamental. It's the underlying system code. Both your users and your AI have to navigate every single day.

takeaways: Intranet search fails because of weak information architecture: global, hub and local navigation, metadata, search and personalization must work together.
Consistent metadata through columns, content types and the term store, plus a flat site structure connected by hubs, is what makes search and Copilot find the right content.
Audience targeting and Viva Connections deliver the right content to the right people, and IA should be tested and refined continuously with card sorting, tree testing and search logs.
hook: Users type the exact document title into your intranet search and still find nothing? This episode is for SharePoint intranet owners, communicators and admins who want content people and Copilot can actually find. Learn how navigation, metadata, flat hub-based sites and audience targeting fix findability.
